metadata.name: NDA & Patent Law Complete Reference — 2026 Edition
metadata.purpose: Complete knowledge map of NDA and Patent law as of January 2026. Includes USPTO guidance, recent Federal Circuit decisions (LKQ, McFadden, USAA v PNC), whistleblower protections, and provisional patent filing strategies. Load this to make any LLM an instant IP law expert for self-filing provisional patents.

canonical_definitions.definition: Statutory requirement that patents cover 'any new and useful process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter.' Subject to judicial exceptions: abstract ideas, laws of nature, natural phenomena (Alice/Mayo test).

Step 1: Is claim directed to abstract idea/law of nature/natural phenomenon? Step 2: Does claim contain inventive concept that transforms it into patent-eligible application? USPTO 2024 guidance clarifies AI inventions often qualify as 'improvements to computer functioning.'
notes: August 2025 memo clarifies mental process limits and practical application integration

canonical_definitions.definition: Non-examined patent filing establishing priority date. Must include: (1) written description enabling person skilled in art to make/use invention, (2) drawings if necessary, (3) cover sheet, (4) filing fee. Valid for 12 months; must file non-provisional to maintain rights.
80% fee discount for applicants meeting: (1) ≤4 prior applications, (2) income <$251,190 (2025 limit), (3) no assignment to large entity. False claims subject to penalty as of 2025.
notes: Income limit adjusted annually; was $251,190 as of September 9, 2025

canonical_definitions.definition: Patent specification must describe invention in sufficient detail for person of ordinary skill in art (POSITA) to make and use it without undue experimentation. Critical for provisional patents.

Four-factor test for obviousness under 35 USC 103: (1) scope/content of prior art, (2) differences between prior art and claimed invention, (3) level of ordinary skill, (4) secondary considerations (commercial success, long-felt need, etc.). As of May 2024 (LKQ Corp v GM), applies to BOTH utility AND design patents.
notes: LKQ overruled 40-year Rosen-Durling test for design patents

canonical_definitions.definition: Information disclosed under NDA that: (1) is identified as confidential, (2) has economic value from secrecy, (3) is subject to reasonable efforts to maintain secrecy. Must be specific; overbroad definitions render NDA unenforceable.

NDAs CANNOT prohibit reporting violations to: SEC, CFTC, DOJ, OSHA, CFPB, or other regulatory agencies. NDAs with such restrictions are unenforceable AND illegal (Rule 21F-17). As of 2024-2025, DOJ/OSHA actively enforce.
notes: SEC settled $3M+ with 7 companies in Sept 2024 for violating Rule 21F-17

canonical_definitions.definition: Under AIA, inventor has 12 months from public disclosure to file patent. After 12 months, invention becomes prior art and is unpatentable. Public disclosure includes: publications, public use, sale/offer for sale, GitHub commits (if public).

Search of existing patents, publications, products to determine if invention is novel and non-obvious. Critical before filing. Sources: USPTO database, Google Patents, academic papers, products in market.

Writing patent claims that define invention scope. Broader claims = more coverage but easier to invalidate. Narrower claims = harder to invalidate but less coverage. Provisionals don't require formal claims but benefit from draft claims.

Independent claim stands alone (Claim 1: A system comprising...). Dependent claim references another claim (Claim 2: The system of claim 1, wherein...). Dependent claims narrow scope and provide fallback if independent claim invalidated.

Written description portion of patent application. Must include: (1) title, (2) field of invention, (3) background, (4) summary, (5) detailed description, (6) claims (for non-provisional). Provisionals need (1-5) only.

Visual representations required when necessary to understand invention. Must show every feature in claims. Provisionals accept informal drawings; non-provisionals require formal drawings per 37 CFR 1.84.
Process of negotiating with USPTO examiner to get patent granted. Includes: office action responses, claim amendments, interviews. Average time: 24-36 months. Starts after non-provisional filing.

USPTO 2024 guidance: AI inventions generally considered computer-implemented inventions. Eligible if claims show: (1) improvement to computer functioning, OR (2) improvement to another technology/technical field. Examples 47-49 illustrate anomaly detection (eligible), speech separation (eligible), personalized medicine (eligible if tied to specific technical implementation).
notes: Recentive Analytics v Fox (Apr 2025): ML for TV scheduling held INELIGIBLE as abstract idea without inventive concept

canonical_definitions.definition: In re McFadden (Sept 2025) reversed PTAB rejection, marking major victory for software patents. Federal Circuit distinguished impermissible mixed system/method claims from permissible system capability claims. PTAB now reverses §101 rejections at 29% rate (up from 8-12% in 2024).
notes: Trend: Software patents strengthening in 2024-2025 if claims show specific technical solutions

patent_eligibility.holding: Software claims directed to abstract idea (intermediated settlement) ineligible without inventive concept

patent_eligibility.case: Mayo Collaborative Services v Prometheus Labs
patent_eligibility.holding: Claims to natural phenomena (metabolite correlations) ineligible
patent_eligibility.impact: Established that laws of nature + routine steps = ineligible

patent_eligibility.holding: ML models for TV broadcast scheduling ineligible as abstract idea
patent_eligibility.impact: First major Federal Circuit AI/ML §101 ruling; reinforces need for technical improvement claims

patent_eligibility.holding: $218.5M verdict reversed; remote check deposit patents ineligible as abstract idea
patent_eligibility.impact: Major software patent defeat; emphasizes need for specific technical solutions beyond generic functions

patent_eligibility.holding: Reversed PTAB §101 rejection of computer system claims
patent_eligibility.impact: Major software patent victory; clarified system capability claims are permissible

obviousness.holding: Rejected rigid teaching-suggestion-motivation test; obviousness requires flexible analysis
obviousness.impact: Made it easier to invalidate patents as obvious

obviousness.case: LKQ Corp v GM Global Technology Operations
obviousness.holding: Overruled Rosen-Durling test for design patents; Graham factors now apply to design AND utility patents
obviousness.impact: MAJOR: 40 years of design patent precedent overturned; Graham factors universal
notes: May cause 'brief period of uncertainty' per Federal Circuit; PTAB issued first post-LKQ decision Aug 2024

nda_whistleblower.holding: NDAs violated Rule 21F-17(a) by impeding SEC communication
Employee NDAs impeded CFTC communication ability
nda_whistleblower.impact: CFTC actively enforcing against restrictive NDAs

techniques_reference.label: Provisional Patent Drafting
failure_modes: Missing claims coverage (can't add later in non-provisional)
steps: 9. Micro Entity Declaration (Form SB/15A if qualifying)

techniques_reference.label: Prior Art Search
failure_modes: Missing key prior art (can invalidate patent later)

techniques_reference.label: NDA Drafting (2025 Compliant)
failure_modes: Unreasonable duration (2-5 years typical; >10 years risky)
required_clauses: 1. Definition of Confidential Information (specific, not overbroad)
3. Exclusions (publicly available, independently developed, legally compelled)
techniques_reference.whistleblower_template: Nothing in this Agreement prohibits Employee from reporting possible violations of law or regulation to any governmental agency or entity, or from making other disclosures protected under whistleblower provisions of applicable law or regulation. Employee does not need prior authorization to make such reports or disclosures and is not required to notify Company of such reports or disclosures.

techniques_reference.label: Adversarial Patent Review
steps: 1. Load draft into LLM with IP law cogni map
2. Prompt: 'You are a patent examiner. Find weaknesses under Alice/Mayo, Graham, and enablement requirements.'
3. Prompt: 'You are opposing counsel. Find prior art that invalidates these claims.'
6. Repeat until adversarial review finds no major gaps

techniques_reference.label: AI Patent §101 Eligibility Analysis (2024 Guidance)
failure_modes: Over-reliance on 2024 examples without case-specific analysis
steps: 1. Identify if claim directed to abstract idea (Step 1 of Alice/Mayo)
2. If yes, determine if improvement to: (a) computer functioning, OR (b) another technology/technical field
4. Draft claims emphasizing technical improvements, not generic ML/AI concepts
5. Avoid: 'using AI to...', 'applying ML to...' (too abstract)
6. Prefer: 'computer system with neural network architecture X that reduces computation by Y%' (technical improvement)

red_team_challenges.attack: Inventor files provisional with vague description. Later, when filing non-provisional, realizes key feature wasn't described. Non-provisional can't claim it (no support in provisional).
defense: Draft detailed claims in provisional even though not required
Describe invention from multiple angles (system, method, apparatus)
Include variations and alternatives
Run adversarial review before filing

red_team_challenges.attack: Examiner issues Alice/Mayo rejection: 'Claims directed to abstract idea of [X] using generic computer components.'
defense: Emphasize specific technical improvements per 2024 USPTO guidance
Cite Examples 47-49 in arguments
Show improvement to computer functioning (speed, memory, accuracy)
Avoid mental process language ('analyzing', 'determining', 'identifying' without technical detail)
Include architectural details (neural network structure, algorithm specifics)

red_team_challenges.attack: Competitor finds prior art (patent, publication, product) that anticipates or makes obvious your claims.
defense: Comprehensive prior art search BEFORE filing
Search patents, academic papers, products, GitHub repos
Document search in invention disclosure
Draft narrow dependent claims as fallback
Include secondary considerations (commercial success, long-felt need) in prosecution

red_team_challenges.attack: Employee signs NDA with broad non-disclosure clause. Later reports securities violation to SEC. Company sues for NDA breach. SEC investigates company for Rule 21F-17 violation.
defense: ALWAYS include whistleblower carve-out in NDAs (see T:NdaDrafting template)
Review existing NDAs for compliance with 2024-2025 guidance
Train HR/legal on DOJ/OSHA enforcement actions
Avoid language that 'may intimidate employees' per CFPB

red_team_challenges.attack: Inventor publishes invention on GitHub, gives conference talk, or sells product. Forgets to file patent within 12 months. Invention becomes prior art; patent barred.
defense: File provisional BEFORE any public disclosure (safest)
If disclosed, calendar 12-month deadline immediately
Public disclosure includes: publications, GitHub commits (public repos), sales, conference talks, product launches
When in doubt, file provisional early (only $130 for micro entity)

red_team_challenges.attack: Examiner rejects: 'Specification does not enable person skilled in art to make/use invention without undue experimentation.'
defense: Include detailed implementation steps in provisional
Add code snippets, algorithms, architectural diagrams
Define terms that may be ambiguous to POSITA
Include working examples if possible
Describe failure modes and how to overcome them

red_team_challenges.threat: Design Patent Obviousness Under New Graham Test
red_team_challenges.attack: Post-LKQ (May 2024), examiner applies Graham factors to design patent. Finds prior art references that, in combination, suggest claimed design. Rejects as obvious under §103.
defense: Understand LKQ overruled Rosen-Durling; Graham now applies to design patents
Emphasize unique visual impression (not just combination of known elements)
Show secondary considerations (commercial success, design awards, copying by competitors)
Distinguish from prior art based on overall visual impression
Note: Some uncertainty remains; PTAB issued first post-LKQ decision Aug 2024

file_provisional_checklist: ☐ Specification written (Title, Field, Background, Summary, Detailed Description)
☐ Draft claims written (recommended even if not required)
☐ Micro Entity Declaration (Form SB/15A) if qualifying
☐ Fee paid ($130 micro entity, $300 small entity, $600 large entity)
nda_compliance_checklist: ☐ Exclusions for publicly available info, independently developed
☐ No restrictions on reporting to SEC, CFTC, DOJ, OSHA, CFPB
ai_patent_drafting_tips: ✓ Include architectural details (neural network structure, layers, parameters)
✓ Show how invention improves computer functioning
✓ Avoid generic AI/ML language ('using machine learning to...')
✓ Include specific algorithms, training methods, data structures
✗ Don't claim mental processes without technical integration
✗ Don't rely on abstract ideas (optimize, analyze, determine) without technical detail
key_deadlines: 12 months: File non-provisional after provisional (or lose priority)
12 months: File patent after public disclosure (or lose rights)
20 months: File PCT if seeking international protection
Annual: Micro entity income limit adjusted (check USPTO.gov)

common_pitfalls.why_fails: Non-provisional can't claim features not enabled in provisional
common_pitfalls.fix: Include detailed implementation in provisional; describe how POSITA would make/use invention

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Using generic AI language in claims
common_pitfalls.why_fails: Examiner issues Alice rejection for abstract idea
common_pitfalls.fix: Emphasize specific technical improvements per USPTO 2024 guidance; cite Examples 47-49

common_pitfalls.why_fails: Violates Rule 21F-17; illegal and unenforceable; DOJ/OSHA may penalize
common_pitfalls.fix: Add mandatory whistleblower clause to all NDAs (see T:NdaDrafting template)

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Publishing on GitHub before filing patent
common_pitfalls.why_fails: Starts 12-month statutory bar clock; miss deadline = lose patent rights
common_pitfalls.fix: File provisional BEFORE any public disclosure; or calendar 12-month deadline religiously

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Assuming design patent obviousness test hasn't changed
common_pitfalls.why_fails: LKQ (May 2024) overruled Rosen-Durling; Graham factors now apply
common_pitfalls.fix: Update design patent strategy for post-LKQ regime; emphasize overall visual impression + secondary considerations

validation_qa.question: What are the requirements for micro entity status in 2025?
validation_qa.expected_answer: ≤4 prior applications, income <$251,190 (2025 limit as of Sept 9), no assignment to large entity. Provides 80% fee discount. False claims subject to penalty.

validation_qa.question: Can an NDA prohibit an employee from reporting securities violations to the SEC?
validation_qa.expected_answer: No. NDAs cannot prohibit reporting to SEC, CFTC, or other regulatory agencies per Rule 21F-17. Such restrictions are illegal AND unenforceable. SEC settled with 7 companies for $3M+ in Sept 2024 for violations. NDAs must include whistleblower carve-out.

validation_qa.question: What changed in design patent law in 2024?
validation_qa.expected_answer: LKQ Corp v GM (May 2024) overruled 40-year Rosen-Durling test. Graham factors now apply to design patents (same as utility patents). No longer require primary reference 'basically the same' as claimed design. May cause brief uncertainty; PTAB issued first post-LKQ decision Aug 2024.
references: LKQ Corp v GM, 102 F.4th 1280 (Fed. Cir. 2024)

validation_qa.question: How does USPTO 2024 guidance affect AI patent eligibility?
validation_qa.expected_answer: July 2024 guidance provides Examples 47-49 showing AI inventions eligible if they improve computer functioning or another technical field. August 2025 memo clarifies mental process limits and practical application integration. Many AI claims eligible as 'improvements to functioning of computer.' But see Recentive v Fox (Apr 2025): ML for TV scheduling held ineligible as abstract idea.

validation_qa.question: What happens if I publish my invention on GitHub before filing a patent?
validation_qa.expected_answer: Public disclosure starts 12-month clock under 35 USC 102(b)(1). Must file patent within 12 months or invention becomes prior art and unpatentable. GitHub commits (public repos) count as public disclosure. Safest: file provisional BEFORE any disclosure.

validation_qa.question: What's the difference between a provisional and non-provisional patent application?
validation_qa.expected_answer: Provisional: establishes priority date, not examined, no formal claims required, valid 12 months, $130 micro entity fee. Non-provisional: examined for patentability, requires formal claims, leads to patent grant if approved, must be filed within 12 months of provisional to claim priority.

validation_qa.question: What should I include in a provisional patent application?
validation_qa.expected_answer: Required: (1) written description enabling POSITA to make/use invention, (2) drawings if necessary, (3) cover sheet (Form SB/16), (4) filing fee. Recommended but not required: draft claims. Must satisfy enablement under 35 USC 112(a).

validation_qa.question: What happened in In re McFadden (Sept 2025)?
validation_qa.expected_answer: Federal Circuit reversed PTAB §101 rejection of computer system claims. Major software patent victory. Clarified that system capability claims are permissible (vs impermissible mixed system/method claims). PTAB §101 reversal rate jumped to 29% in Nov 2025 (up from 8-12% in 2024).

validation_qa.question: What are the Graham factors for patent obviousness?
validation_qa.expected_answer: Four factors: (1) scope/content of prior art, (2) differences between prior art and claimed invention, (3) level of ordinary skill in art, (4) secondary considerations (commercial success, long-felt need, failure of others, copying). Established in Graham v John Deere (1966). As of LKQ (May 2024), applies to BOTH utility AND design patents.

validation_qa.question: Can I use my own AI system to draft my provisional patent?
validation_qa.expected_answer: Yes, but risky. Provisionals are forgiving (no formal claims, plain English OK), but must satisfy enablement. Using AI + IP law cogni map can help draft, but run adversarial review to find gaps. Missing critical features = can't add in non-provisional later. Consider it 70-80% as good as lawyer, but saves $2k-$5k.
